label: Late in the original phase of long sequences: <DEL> or one of b/z/0/n/e/q/g/f
explanation: The unit fires almost only during the original phase and on the <DEL> step: 56% of activation mass is in the original phase, 44% on <DEL>, and 0.4% in the copy phase. It never fires at t=0. Firing rate climbs with position, so long sequences dominate: L=9 holds 45% of mass, and the rate at orig_idx 8 is 0.33 versus 0.03-0.04 at positions 1-3. On <DEL> it fires in 25% of all sequences, more often when L is large. In the original phase it prefers a specific set of input tokens: b (3.7x lift), z, 0, n, e, q, g, f. It favours first occurrences (in_first=1 holds 91% of mass) and is mildly raised when the first token is t, d or k. The top examples reach their peak on a set token at the last original position or on <DEL> in L=8-9 sequences, often after a run of active steps. It is suppressed on w, u, h and in the copy phase. The predicate captures about 68% of mass on dev, but precision is only about 0.45, because many long sequences with these tokens late, or with <DEL>, stay below threshold. The neuron seems to integrate graded evidence that no simple predicate fully reproduces.
